rationale: VIVI-OLIVE registers falls and gait for a diet-plus-extra-virgin-oil bundle and has no posted results. An oil grade comparison reports walking speed in sarcopenia. Rotarod studies use olive oil as a shared drug vehicle with unspecified grade. An isolated cold-pressed oil result for clinical Parkinson postural instability remains open.

Concentrated common-sage spray reduced acute sore-throat pain versus its control. A surgery comparison favored benzydamine over sage rinse. The palliative sage-rinse study recorded oral pain at baseline and omitted it from comparisons. High-dose animal safety observations use extract. Fresh dietary sage and clinical Parkinson pain remain unresolved.

The postoperative ginger drink comparison had baseline imbalance. Blinded craniotomy and healthy-adult powder comparisons were inconclusive. The generalized-anxiety abstract is internally inconsistent and the Parkinson extract trial has no posted results. Ginger and ginkgo extracts showed dose-dependent maze effects in rats and differed at 1 mg/kg, leaving freshly grated ginger and clinical anxiety unresolved.
